title: G4 CET Unseen Reading — Reading 3: Chi Po-lin: Seeing Taiwan from Above
examKicker: Tr. Alan / G4 CET Unseen Reading Practice

parts.title: Part A | Reading Comprehension
parts.instruction: Directions: Choose the best answer based on the selection. Fill in one circle for each question.

questions.q: According to paragraph 1, what did Chi's government work involve?
options: Teaching high school students to use cameras.
Building helicopters for environmental projects.
Writing stories about Taiwan's mountain villages.
Photographing major construction projects in Taiwan.

questions.q: Why were photographs taken from the air useful for showing environmental damage?
options: They made every damaged place appear beautiful.
They could reveal how large the problems were.
They allowed Chi to avoid recording human activities.
They showed only places with clean rivers and forests.

questions.q: Which detail best shows Chi's commitment to making documentary films?
options: He began learning photography while in high school.
His government work included construction projects.
He left his government job to focus on filmmaking.
His pictures included mountains and Taiwan's coastlines.

questions.q: Why did Chi include both beautiful and damaged places in his film?
options: To show what Taiwan had and why it needed protection.
To compare Taiwan's scenery with places in other countries.
To explain why photographs were better than moving images.
To prove that people had already solved environmental problems.

questions.q: According to paragraph 5, how did Chi's work continue after his death?
options: His government office completed every film he had planned.
His photographs were used only to record new buildings.
His second film replaced all of his earlier photographs.
His foundation used his images for films and education.

questions.q: Based on the selection, which statement best describes the change in Chi's work?
options: He moved from filming real places to inventing imaginary ones.
He used photography to record places and encourage their protection.
He stopped photographing Taiwan and focused on foreign countries.
He replaced his interest in photography with an interest in construction. 12

parts.readText:
Chi Po-lin: Seeing Taiwan from Above

WORDS TO KNOW
construction - the work of building
landscape - the visible features of land
documentary - a film about real subjects
foundation - an organization supporting a cause

[1] Chi Po-lin began learning photography in high school. He later turned his interest into a career. In 1990, he began working for a government office, taking photographs of major construction projects in Taiwan. His work included photographing the land from the air.

[2] From a helicopter, Chi could record views that were difficult to see from the ground. Over many years, he collected hundreds of thousands of photographs. His pictures recorded Taiwan's mountains, coastlines, and changing landscape.

[3] However, beautiful scenery was only part of the story. Human activities were also damaging the land. Mountains were being dug up for materials, and pollution was entering rivers. A view from above could show the size of these problems. Chi wanted more people to notice what was happening to their home.

[4] Chi left his government job to focus on making documentary films. A documentary presents real people, places, or events. In 2013, his film Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above was released. It showed both Taiwan's natural beauty and the damage caused by human activities. At the end, children sang on a mountain, and the film invited people to work together to improve their home.

[5] The film encouraged public discussion about protecting the environment. Chi later planned a second film. In 2017, he died in a helicopter crash while working on the new project. After his death, the Chi Po-lin Foundation continued using his images for films and environmental education.

[6] Chi's work gave people another way to see Taiwan. His photographs were records of the land, but they also helped people notice why it needed care. Look closely at the place you call home, and take action to protect it.

parts.title: Part B | Short Answer
parts.instruction: Directions: Answer in complete sentences. Support your answers with details from the selection.

questions.q: How did Chi turn a personal interest into work that helped other people understand Taiwan? Use details from the beginning and later parts of the selection.
questions.keyPoints: Beginning: he learned photography in high school and later worked for a government office photographing construction projects from the air (1990). Later: his aerial pictures showed the size of environmental damage, and he left his job to make the documentary Beyond Beauty (2013), which helped people see Taiwan's beauty and the damage so they would care for it.

questions.q: Explain how Chi's film did more than show attractive scenery. Include two details from the selection.
questions.keyPoints: It showed both natural beauty and the damage caused by human activities (mountains dug up, polluted rivers), and it invited people to work together to improve their home — it ended with children singing on a mountain and encouraged public discussion about protecting the environment.

parts.title: Part C | Explain Author's Purpose — Questions 1–3
parts.instruction: Directions: Read each sentence from the selection. Choose its main purpose.

questions.q:
What is the main purpose of this sentence from the selection?
"In 2013, his film Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above was released."
options: Inform
Entertain
Persuade
Express Feelings

questions.q:
What is the main purpose of this sentence from the selection?
"A documentary presents real people, places, or events."
options: Inform
Entertain
Persuade
Express Feelings

questions.q:
What is the main purpose of this sentence from the selection?
"Look closely at the place you call home, and take action to protect it."
options: Inform
Entertain
Persuade
Express Feelings

questions.q:
Choose one sentence above (write its number). Explain how its words help you identify the purpose.
Sentence Number:
questions.keyPoints: e.g. Sentence 3 is to PERSUADE: it is a command ("Look closely… take action") that tells readers what to do, not just a fact. Sentence 1 or 2 is to INFORM: it states a date or a definition as a fact.

questions.q: Why does the author include the information about the foundation in paragraph 5?
options: To explain how readers can apply for a government job.
To compare Chi's photographs with other artists' work.
To show that Chi's work continued to be used after his death.
To describe how the foundation built a new helicopter.

parts.title: Part D | Analyze Text Structure — Number the events 1–5
parts.instruction: Directions: Number the events from 1-5 to show the order in which they happened.
events: Chi began learning photography in high school.
Chi photographed construction projects for a government office.
Chi left his government job to focus on documentary films.
Chi's film Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above was released.
The foundation continued using Chi's images after his death.

questions.q: How is most of this biography organized?
options: It compares the lives of two different photographers.
It presents important events in the order they happened.
It lists environmental problems from largest to smallest.
It gives instructions for making a documentary film.

questions.q: Why is this structure helpful for understanding Chi's life?
options: It lets readers rank his photographs by their beauty.
It helps readers compare Taiwan with other countries.
It shows readers which camera they should buy first.
It shows how his interest developed into lasting work.

questions.q: Explain how Chi's work developed over time. Include one early event and one later event from the selection.
questions.keyPoints: Early (any one): he began learning photography in high school; in 1990 he started photographing construction projects for a government office. Later (any one): he left his job to make documentary films; his film was released in 2013; after he died in 2017 the foundation kept using his images. Strong answers say how it developed: from recording the land to encouraging people to protect it.
